answer: In a market for audio labels, a buyer posts a violet-tagged clip containing the whisper of a falcon call. Agents submit sealed bids with a nonrefundable entry fee and a slashing bond; the contract pays for only one verified label per recording hash. Fifty aliases may buy more chances to win, but they pay fifty fees and cannot turn one clip into fifty rewards. If copied or false work wins, a random audit takes the bond. A wealthy attacker can still flood bids, while hash changes can disguise duplicates, so compare acoustic fingerprints and let disputed matches go to independent review.
